ENVIRONMENTAL_INPUT.description: Physical properties of the architectural environment serving as stimulus inputs

luminance_level.description: Ambient light intensity measured at the eye or surface plane. Encompasses photopic luminance (cone-mediated daytime vision), melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (ipRGC-mediated circadian entrainment), and spectral power distribution including correlated color temperature (CCT). Primary driver of circadian regulation (T1.9 CB), visual prediction error, and alerting responses.
luminance_level.role: Stimulus input that architects directly specify via lighting design. Feeds into circadian entrainment, prediction error, alerting, and visual comfort mechanisms. Primary design lever for health, productivity, and circadian regulation.

spatial_enclosure_ratio.description: The ratio of ceiling height to the square root of floor area (R_h), indexing perceived spatial volume and enclosure. Values below ~2.0 elicit confinement stress via amygdala activation; values in the 2.5-3.5 range optimize the Goldilocks zone for cognitive performance. Mediates the spatial prediction error signal in the predictive processing framework (T1.1 PP).
spatial_enclosure_ratio.role: Stimulus input that architects control via ceiling height and room proportions. Feeds into spatial prediction error, stress/comfort Goldilocks zone, and prospect-refuge balance. Primary design lever for perceived spaciousness.

visual_complexity.description: Information density and structural regularity of the visual field including fractal dimension (D), spatial frequency content (LSF/HSF), curvature statistics, self-similarity at multiple scales, and contour angular properties. Drives visual prediction error magnitude and aesthetic preference via the complexity-compression tradeoff in predictive processing.
visual_complexity.role: Stimulus input controlled via surface patterns, material variety, and formal composition. Feeds into visual prediction error magnitude and aesthetic preference. Primary design lever for interest-vs-overwhelm balance.

nature_view_quality.description: Presence, extent, biodiversity, and layer complexity of visible natural elements from an architectural vantage point. Graded from blank wall (0) through urban views to high-biodiversity natural landscape (1.0). Engages multiple restorative channels: fractal fluency (Channel 1), prospect-refuge geometry (Channel 2), soft fascination (Channel 3), temporal variation (Channel 4), and ecological safety signaling (Channel 5).
nature_view_quality.role: Stimulus input controlled via window placement, landscape design, and interior biophilic elements. Feeds into attention restoration, stress reduction, and circadian entrainment. Primary design lever for occupant wellbeing.

acoustic_environment.description: Acoustic properties of the enclosed environment including background noise level (dB(A)), reverberation time (RT60), speech intelligibility (STI), soundscape composition (biophilic/mechanical/human), and spectral characteristics. Affects auditory scene analysis, cognitive load from masking interference, and circadian alerting via abrupt onset detection.
acoustic_environment.role: Stimulus input controlled via acoustic design (absorption, isolation, masking). Feeds into cognitive load, speech intelligibility, and circadian alerting. Primary design lever for concentration and communication.

thermal_conditions.description: Thermal environment state including operative temperature, mean radiant temperature, air velocity, and humidity. Processed via thermoreceptors and insular cortex interoceptive pathways. Governs thermal comfort (PMV/PPD), allesthesia (thermal pleasure from deviation correction), and metabolic prediction error in the body-budget model (T1.6 IC).
thermal_conditions.role: Stimulus input controlled via HVAC, envelope design, and radiant systems. Feeds into thermal comfort, interoceptive prediction, and allostatic load. Primary design lever for occupant comfort and health.

material_surface_properties.description: Physical and perceptual qualities of surfaces including roughness, thermal effusivity (warm/cool to touch), naturalness, visual grain, and patina/aging depth. Processed through haptic exploration (C-tactile afferents for pleasant touch), visual texture statistics, and cross-modal material identity integration (T1.10 MSI).
material_surface_properties.role: Stimulus input controlled via material specification and detailing. Feeds into haptic processing, cross-modal integration, and affective appraisal. Primary design lever for tactile richness and material warmth.

spatial_configuration.description: Topological and metric properties of architectural layout measured via space syntax (integration, connectivity, intelligibility), isovist analysis (visible area, compactness, occlusivity), and wayfinding affordances. Determines movement patterns, encounter probabilities, and cognitive mapping difficulty. Core input to spatial navigation mechanisms (T1.2 SN).
spatial_configuration.role: Stimulus input controlled via plan layout and spatial connectivity. Feeds into wayfinding, movement patterns, and social encounter probability. Primary design lever for building usability and social interaction.

color_properties.description: Chromatic characteristics of surfaces and light including hue angle, chroma/saturation, lightness, and warm-cool spectral balance. Processed via opponent-channel mechanisms and associated with cross-modal correspondences, cultural evaluative conditioning, and arousal modulation.
color_properties.role: Stimulus input controlled via color palette selection. Feeds into arousal modulation, cross-modal associations, and cultural evaluative conditioning. Supporting design lever for mood and identity.

olfactory_environment.description: Airborne chemical stimuli processed via olfactory receptor neurons with direct projections to amygdala and hippocampus (bypassing thalamic relay). Uniquely potent for episodic memory retrieval (Proust effect) and affective state modulation. Relevant for transition marking and place identity.
olfactory_environment.role: Stimulus input partially controlled via ventilation, material off-gassing, and planting. Feeds into episodic memory formation and affective state. Indirect design lever; most impact via eliminating negative odors.

interpersonal_distance.description: Physical distance between persons categorized by Hall's proxemic zones: intimate (<0.45m), personal (0.45-1.2m), social (1.2-3.7m), and public (>3.7m). Architecturally mediated by furniture arrangement, visual barriers, and spatial configuration. Violation of expected zone triggers amygdala threat response and autonomic arousal.
interpersonal_distance.role: Stimulus input controlled via furniture layout and spatial dimensioning. Feeds into proxemic comfort, territorial stress, and oxytocin/cortisol balance. Primary design lever for social comfort.

temporal_rhythm.description: Time-varying properties of environmental stimulation including diurnal light cycles, ultradian activity-rest patterns, event boundaries, and transition frequencies. Engages circadian oscillators (SCN), episodic memory segmentation (hippocampal boundary detection), and temporal prediction in the predictive processing hierarchy.
temporal_rhythm.role: Stimulus input controlled via dynamic lighting, program scheduling, and spatial sequencing. Feeds into circadian entrainment, episodic segmentation, and restorative cycling. Design lever for temporal wellbeing.

architectural_threshold.description: Physical boundaries and transitions between architectural spaces: doorways, corridors, level changes, material transitions. Triggers episodic boundary encoding (doorway effect) in hippocampus, increases prediction error at spatial transitions, and segments experience into discrete episodes for memory consolidation.
architectural_threshold.role: Stimulus input controlled via transition design (doors, corridors, level changes). Feeds into episodic memory segmentation and prediction error at boundaries. Design lever for spatial narrative and wayfinding.

privacy_gradient.description: Degree of visual, acoustic, and social shielding afforded by architectural boundary conditions. Parametrized by edge sharpness, visual penetration depth, acoustic isolation (STC rating), and controllability of boundaries. Governs privacy regulation (Altman's dialectic model) and territorial stress.
privacy_gradient.role: Stimulus input controlled via boundary design, visual barriers, and zoning. Feeds into perceived control, territorial regulation, and social withdrawal options. Primary design lever for privacy-sociality balance.

territorial_markers.description: Environmental cues signaling ownership, group membership, and social hierarchy boundaries. Includes personalization, boundary markers, and Dunbar-scale spatial allocation (5→15→50→150 person group layers). Modulates oxytocin-mediated in-group bonding and cortisol-mediated boundary defense.
territorial_markers.role: Stimulus input controlled via personalization opportunities and group-scaled spaces. Feeds into oxytocin-mediated bonding and cortisol boundary defense. Design lever for social group coherence.

environmental_novelty_level.description: Degree to which current environmental configuration deviates from the brain's generative model predictions. Drives dopaminergic exploration-exploitation tradeoff (T1.5 NM) and determines whether the environment triggers approach (moderate novelty) or avoidance (excessive novelty) behavior.
environmental_novelty_level.role: Stimulus input controlled via design variation, surprise elements, and spatial sequencing. Feeds into dopaminergic exploration drive and prediction error. Design lever for engagement and curiosity.

musical_stimulus.description: Properties of musical or structured acoustic stimulation including tempo (BPM), rhythmic complexity (syncopation), melodic contour, harmonic tension, spectral flux, and familiarity. Engages BRECVEMA multi-mechanism emotional processing, motor entrainment, and reward prediction through expectancy violation.
musical_stimulus.role: Stimulus input controlled via sound system design and programming. Feeds into emotional processing, motor entrainment, and reward. Design lever for atmosphere and temporal experience.

movement_affordances.description: Environmental support for physical movement including walkable path networks, stairway design, ramp gradients, and promenade sequences. Supports creative incubation (walking boosts divergent thinking ~60%), motor-proprioceptive enrichment, and embodied spatial cognition (T1.8 EC).
movement_affordances.role: Stimulus input controlled via circulation design, stairway prominence, and path networks. Feeds into creative incubation, embodied cognition, and physical health. Design lever for active design.

social_setting_features.description: Architectural features that structure social interaction: co-presence affordances, visual body access conditions, seating arrangements, shared activity zones, and encounter density gradients. Determines social contact frequency, quality, and valence through space syntax integration values and affordance density.
social_setting_features.role: Stimulus input controlled via seating arrangement, visual access, and encounter density. Feeds into social contact frequency, quality, and oxytocin release. Primary design lever for community building.

safety_threat_cues.description: Environmental features signaling safety (open sightlines, adequate lighting, visible exits, social co-presence) or threat (concealed approaches, entrapment geometry, sudden acoustic events). Processed via the fast subcortical amygdala pathway and modulated by architectural prospect-refuge configuration.
safety_threat_cues.role: Stimulus input controlled via sightline design, lighting adequacy, and exit visibility. Feeds into amygdala threat response and vagal regulation. Primary design lever for occupant security.

sensory_input_generic.description: Multi-modal sensory input that does not map to a single modality. Used for cross-cutting variables that span visual, auditory, haptic, olfactory, and proprioceptive channels simultaneously.
sensory_input_generic.role: Catch-all for multi-modal sensory inputs that span several channels simultaneously. Used when a template mechanism references general sensory richness without specifying modality.

NEURAL_MECHANISM.description: Neural processes mediating between environmental input and psychological/behavioral outcomes

prediction_error_signal.description: The discrepancy between the brain's generative model prediction and incoming sensory evidence, computed at every level of the cortical hierarchy. Unsigned PE drives attention and learning; signed PE drives model updating. The core computational currency of predictive processing (T1.1 PP). Architectural features that generate moderate PE are experienced as interesting; excessive PE as stressful.
prediction_error_signal.role: Core computational currency of the CMR. Every environmental input generates PE at some level. The magnitude and sign of PE determines whether an environment is experienced as boring (zero PE), interesting (moderate PE), or stressful (excessive PE). Templates use this to predict the neural response to a design feature.

dopaminergic_response.description: Midbrain dopaminergic system activation (VTA → nucleus accumbens, PFC) encoding reward prediction error, incentive salience ('wanting'), and approach motivation. Separate from hedonic impact ('liking', mediated by opioid hotspots). Environmental novelty and positive prediction error drive phasic DA release; saturation and predictability suppress it.
dopaminergic_response.role: Mediates reward processing and approach motivation. Templates use this to predict whether a design feature will be experienced as rewarding/attractive (positive RPE) or neutral/aversive (negative RPE). Links to behavioral outcomes like exploration, dwell time, and preference.

noradrenergic_response.description: Locus coeruleus-norepinephrine (LC-NE) system controlling arousal level and the explore-exploit tradeoff. Tonic high NE promotes exploitation of known affordances; phasic NE bursts promote exploratory shifts. Regulates cortical signal-to-noise ratio and attentional gating. Activated by environmental uncertainty and salience.
noradrenergic_response.role: Mediates arousal regulation and the explore-exploit tradeoff. Templates use this to predict whether an environment will promote alertness and exploration (phasic NE) or focused sustained attention (tonic NE). Links environmental uncertainty to cognitive strategy.

cholinergic_response.description: Basal forebrain acetylcholine (ACh) system projecting to cortex, modulating precision weighting of sensory evidence relative to prior predictions. High ACh increases the gain on bottom-up sensory signals (useful in novel/uncertain environments); low ACh allows top-down priors to dominate (familiar environments).
cholinergic_response.role: Mediates precision weighting of sensory evidence. Templates use this to model how novel vs. familiar environments shift the balance between bottom-up perception and top-down expectation. Critical for explaining expertise and familiarity effects.

hpa_axis_activation.description: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis stress cascade: environmental threat cues → amygdala → hypothalamus → CRH → pituitary ACTH → adrenal cortisol. Acute activation is adaptive; chronic activation produces allostatic load, hippocampal dendritic retraction, and immunosuppression. Architectural entrapment and uncontrollable noise are potent triggers.
hpa_axis_activation.role: Mediates the stress response pathway. Templates use this to predict cortisol output from architectural stressors (noise, crowding, entrapment). Links to allostatic load accumulation and long-term health outcomes. Key mechanism for 'unhealthy building' claims.

vagal_regulation.description: Cardiac vagal tone (indexed by respiratory sinus arrhythmia, RMSSD) reflecting parasympathetic nervous system state. High vagal tone indicates a neurophysiological state conducive to social engagement, emotional regulation, and calm exploration. Architectural safety signals (open prospect, social co-presence at appropriate density) increase vagal tone via ventral vagal complex.
vagal_regulation.role: Mediates parasympathetic safety signaling. Templates use this to predict whether architectural features will promote calm engagement (high vagal tone) or defensive arousal (vagal withdrawal). Key mechanism for restorative and healing environment claims.

oxytocin_system.description: Oxytocinergic system mediating social bonding, trust, and prosocial behavior. Released under conditions of positive social contact, eye contact at appropriate distance, and shared activity in safe environments. Architectural features promoting oxytocin release include communal dining configurations, face-to-face seating at personal-zone distances, and shared prospect views.
oxytocin_system.role: Mediates social bonding physiology. Templates use this to predict whether architectural social affordances will promote trust, affiliation, and prosocial behavior. Links spatial design to community health outcomes via neuroendocrine pathways.

allostatic_load.description: Cumulative physiological cost of chronic environmental demands that exceed the body's regulatory capacity. Indexed by composite biomarkers (cortisol diurnal slope, inflammatory markers, metabolic syndrome indicators, cardiovascular risk). The master integrating variable for environmental health impact — all environmental stressors ultimately feed into allostatic load accumulation.
allostatic_load.role: Master integrating variable for chronic environmental health impact. All stressor inputs (noise, thermal extremes, social isolation, circadian disruption) accumulate here. Templates use this to make long-term health predictions from sustained exposure to building conditions.

dmn_tpn_balance.description: Dynamic anti-correlation between the Default Mode Network (midline structures, lateral parietal for self-referential processing, mind-wandering, consolidation) and Task-Positive Networks (dorsal attention, frontoparietal control for focused external task performance). Sustained TPN engagement suppresses DMN = 'directed attention fatigue' (T1.4 DT). Restorative environments allow DMN re-engagement.
dmn_tpn_balance.role: Mediates attention mode switching. Templates use this to predict whether an environment supports cognitive recovery (DMN re-engagement) or efficient task performance (TPN dominance). Key mechanism for attention restoration and productivity claims.

hippocampal_encoding.description: Hippocampal mechanisms for rapid episodic memory formation: CA3 pattern completion (retrieving full episode from partial cue), dentate gyrus pattern separation (distinguishing similar episodes), and relational binding (linking co-occurring elements). Environmental distinctiveness, novelty, and spatial configuration all modulate encoding strength (T1.7 MS).
hippocampal_encoding.role: Mediates memory formation quality. Templates use this to predict how well experiences in a space will be encoded as lasting memories. Links environmental distinctiveness, novelty, and spatial configuration to memory strength.

memory_consolidation.description: Transfer of hippocampal episodic traces to neocortical semantic memory via systems-level consolidation. Requires sharp-wave ripple replay during rest and sleep. Environmental rest periods and restorative spaces support offline memory consolidation. Schema-congruent experiences consolidate faster via direct neocortical pathways.
memory_consolidation.role: Mediates transfer from hippocampal to neocortical memory. Templates use this to predict how rest spaces and overnight consolidation will stabilize environmental learning. Links architectural rest affordances to learning outcomes.

interoceptive_signal.description: Signals from the body's internal milieu (cardiac, respiratory, gastrointestinal, thermoregulatory) processed by insular cortex, forming the physiological basis for constructed affect and emotional experience. The body-budget model (T1.6 IC): the brain continuously predicts and regulates body states; interoceptive prediction error drives affective experience.
interoceptive_signal.role: Mediates affect construction from bodily signals. Templates use this to model how thermal, visceral, and cardiac interoception contribute to the 'feeling' of being in a space. Core mechanism for the body-budget theory of environmental affect.

mirror_system_activation.description: Neural systems activated during both action execution and action observation (mirror neurons, mentalizing network including TPJ and mPFC). Mediates embodied social cognition, empathy, and architectural affordance reading. Social spaces that enable visual body access and movement observation activate these systems more strongly.
mirror_system_activation.role: Mediates social embodied cognition. Templates use this to predict how architectural visual access to others' bodies and actions affects empathy, social learning, and affordance reading. Links visibility design to social cognitive outcomes.

circadian_entrainment.description: Synchronization of the master circadian pacemaker (SCN) to the 24-hour light-dark cycle via melanopsin-expressing intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs). Determines melatonin onset timing, cortisol awakening response, and cognitive performance rhythms. Architectural lighting design is the primary controllable circadian zeitgeber (T1.9 CB).
circadian_entrainment.role: Mediates biological clock synchronization. Templates use this to quantify how lighting design (melanopic lux, timing, duration) will shift circadian phase. Links architectural lighting to sleep, alertness, and metabolic health.

multisensory_integration.description: Neural processes combining information across sensory modalities governed by principles of inverse effectiveness (weakest channels benefit most), temporal and spatial coincidence, and Bayesian causal inference (inferring common vs. separate causes). Cross-modal congruency enhances processing fluency and affect; incongruency generates prediction error (T1.10 MSI).
multisensory_integration.role: Mediates cross-modal binding. Templates use this to predict how congruent vs. incongruent multi-channel environments will affect processing fluency and affect. Key mechanism for coherent/incoherent design quality claims.

prefrontal_executive_control.description: PFC-mediated top-down cognitive control including working memory maintenance (dorsolateral PFC), response inhibition (right inferior frontal gyrus), conflict monitoring (ACC/pre-SMA), and task switching. Environmental cognitive load depletes executive resources; restorative environments allow prefrontal recovery.
prefrontal_executive_control.role: Mediates top-down cognitive control resources. Templates use this to predict how environmental demands deplete or preserve working memory, inhibition, and cognitive flexibility. Links environmental complexity to task performance via executive resource depletion.

sensorimotor_coupling.description: Bidirectional coupling between motor systems and spatial perception: environmental affordances are perceived in terms of action possibilities (T1.8 EC). Includes grip scaling, postural adjustments, and simulated actions during architectural navigation. Sensorimotor predictions shape the experience of space through embodied simulation.
sensorimotor_coupling.role: Mediates embodied spatial perception. Templates use this to model how movement through space shapes spatial understanding and affordance perception. Key mechanism for active design and kinesthetic architecture claims.

creative_network_dynamics.description: Large-scale brain network dynamics underlying creative cognition, especially DMN-ECN coupling (idea generation + evaluation), salience network switching, and incubation via default mode processing. Environmental conditions modulating creativity include moderate complexity (Goldilocks zone), movement affordances, and spaces supporting both focused and diffuse attention.
creative_network_dynamics.role: Mediates creative cognition. Templates use this to predict how environmental conditions (complexity, movement, social density) modulate DMN-ECN coupling for creative output. Links workspace design to innovation metrics.

inflammatory_markers.description: Peripheral inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, CRP, TNF-α) reflecting immune system activation from chronic environmental stress. Elevated by social isolation, noise exposure, poor sleep architecture, and sedentary behavior in built environments. Component of allostatic load with downstream effects on neurogenesis, mood, and cardiovascular risk.
inflammatory_markers.role: Mediates immune-mediated health pathway. Templates use this to predict chronic inflammatory burden from environmental stressors (noise, isolation, poor air quality). Links building conditions to cardiovascular and metabolic disease risk.

autonomic_regulation.description: Overall autonomic nervous system balance between sympathetic (fight-or-flight) and parasympathetic (rest-and-digest) branches. Indexed by heart rate variability, pupil diameter, and galvanic skin response. Environmental safety and comfort shift the balance toward parasympathetic dominance; threat and discomfort shift toward sympathetic.
autonomic_regulation.role: Mediates overall sympatho-vagal balance. Templates use this as a general-purpose autonomic variable when the specific neuromodulatory system (NE, ACh, vagal) is not specified. Links environmental safety/threat to physiological state.

PSYCHOLOGICAL_STATE.description: Subjective psychological states resulting from environmental-neural processing

perceived_restorativeness.description: Subjective assessment of an environment's capacity to restore depleted attentional resources, measured by the Perceived Restorativeness Scale (PRS). Components: fascination (effortless attention capture), being-away (psychological distance from demands), extent (scope for exploration), and compatibility (fit between environment and purpose). Core construct of Attention Restoration Theory.
perceived_restorativeness.role: Self-reported outcome measure. Templates targeting attention restoration predict PRS scores. Used to evaluate restorative environment claims and compare design alternatives for stress-recovery spaces (hospitals, parks, break rooms).

emotional_valence.description: The pleasure-displeasure dimension of affective experience, ranging from strongly negative (aversive, fearful) through neutral to strongly positive (pleasurable, delightful). Constructed from interoceptive predictions and environmental appraisals. Architectural settings modulate valence through aesthetic properties, thermal comfort, and social affordances.
emotional_valence.role: Core affect outcome. Templates predict whether a design will produce positive or negative emotional experience. Used to evaluate hedonic design claims and optimize environments for occupant satisfaction and wellbeing.

arousal_level.description: The activation dimension of core affect, from calm/sleepy to excited/alert. Indexed physiologically by skin conductance, pupil dilation, and heart rate. Moderate arousal optimizes cognitive performance (Yerkes-Dodson); excessive arousal from environmental overstimulation degrades performance and wellbeing.
arousal_level.role: Core affect outcome (activation dimension). Templates predict arousal from environmental stimulation. Used to calibrate environments to optimal arousal for their intended activity (calm for rest, moderate for work, high for exercise).

cognitive_load.description: The amount of working memory and attentional resources consumed by environmental processing demands. High cognitive load from complex wayfinding, noise interference, or visual clutter reduces capacity for primary tasks. Processing fluency (ease of environmental comprehension) is the inverse: fluent environments impose lower cognitive load.
cognitive_load.role: Information processing outcome. Templates predict cognitive demand imposed by environmental processing. Used to evaluate wayfinding difficulty, information overload, and the efficiency of spatial design for task support.

perceived_control.description: The subjective sense of being able to influence, modify, or escape environmental conditions. A key moderator of stress responses: identical environmental stressors produce much larger HPA activation and allostatic load when uncontrollable. Architectural features supporting perceived control include adjustable lighting, operable windows, and privacy boundaries.
perceived_control.role: Appraisal outcome and key stress moderator. Templates predict whether occupants will feel able to regulate their environmental conditions. Used to evaluate adjustability, escape options, and privacy boundaries in environmental design.

place_attachment.description: Emotional and functional bond between a person and a specific place, comprising place identity (self-definition through place) and place dependence (functional utility). Develops through repeated positive experiences, personalization, and social associations. Mediates environmental stewardship behavior and resistance to relocation.
place_attachment.role: Long-term affective outcome. Templates predict bond formation between person and place. Used to evaluate designs for residential, community, and institutional settings where occupant retention and stewardship matter.

perceived_safety.description: Subjective feeling of physical and social security in an environment. Driven by prospect-refuge geometry, lighting adequacy, sightline depth, and social co-presence at appropriate density. Prerequisite for exploration, social engagement, and environmental restoration — unsafe environments lock the nervous system in sympathetic vigilance.
perceived_safety.role: Appraisal outcome and prerequisite for all other benefits. Templates predict subjective safety from prospect-refuge geometry and surveillance quality. Used to evaluate designs for public spaces, healthcare, and urban environments.

aesthetic_judgment.description: Evaluative assessment of environmental beauty, harmony, and visual pleasure. Multi-component: prototype matching (familiarity), novelty detection (surprise), processing fluency (ease), and sensory richness. Correlates with visual fractal dimension, proportional harmony (golden ratio approximation), and coherent spatial order.
aesthetic_judgment.role: Evaluative outcome. Templates predict aesthetic preference and beauty ratings. Used to optimize visual design parameters (fractal dimension, proportional harmony, material quality) for maximum aesthetic impact.

awe_experience.description: The emotion of awe triggered by perceived vastness (physical, temporal, or conceptual) that challenges existing mental schemas (need for accommodation). Produces the 'small self' state: reduced self-focus, increased prosocial behavior, and expanded time perception. Architectural triggers include extreme height, dramatic views, and sacred geometry.
awe_experience.role: Peak emotional outcome. Templates predict awe induction from spatial vastness and schema challenge. Used to evaluate designs for sacred spaces, museums, monumental architecture, and spaces intended for transcendent experience.

social_connectedness.description: Subjective experience of meaningful social connection (vs. loneliness/isolation). Mediates the relationship between architectural social affordances and health outcomes. Chronic social isolation produces neuroendocrine cascades (elevated cortisol, inflammatory markers, reduced vagal tone) comparable in health risk to smoking.
social_connectedness.role: Social wellbeing outcome. Templates predict subjective social connection vs. isolation. Used to evaluate designs for community spaces, shared housing, and workplaces where social health is a priority.

thermal_comfort.description: Multi-dimensional subjective assessment of the thermal environment including thermal sensation (ASHRAE 7-point scale), thermal acceptability, and thermal pleasure (alliesthesia — pleasure from returning to thermal setpoint). Modulated by metabolic rate, clothing, adaptive expectations, and personal control over thermal conditions.
thermal_comfort.role: Comfort outcome. Templates predict thermal satisfaction from environmental thermal conditions. Used to evaluate HVAC and envelope design alternatives and optimize energy-comfort tradeoffs.

sense_of_coherence.description: Perceived orderliness, readability, and predictability of an environment. High coherence reduces cognitive load and supports efficient spatial navigation. Related to Kaplan's environmental preference framework where coherence and legibility predict preference for settings that are easy to understand and act within.
sense_of_coherence.role: Cognitive appraisal outcome. Templates predict environmental readability and orderliness. Used to evaluate legibility of spatial design and its impact on wayfinding ease and cognitive efficiency.

task_performance.description: Measurable cognitive task outcomes: accuracy, reaction time, sustained attention duration, and productivity metrics. Modulated by environmental conditions (noise, light, temperature, visual complexity) through their effects on arousal, executive function, and cognitive load. Primary applied outcome measure for evidence-based design.
task_performance.role: Terminal outcome measure. The bottom-line productivity metric that templates predict from environmental conditions. Used to make evidence-based design claims about workspace optimization for cognitive task support.

creative_output.description: Divergent thinking performance (fluency, originality, flexibility on tasks like the Alternative Uses Task) and convergent creative problem solving. Environmental modulators include ceiling height (spaciousness → abstract thinking), moderate noise (processing disfluency → broader associative search), and movement affordances (walking → ~60% divergent thinking boost).
creative_output.role: Terminal outcome measure. Templates predict divergent/convergent thinking performance from environmental conditions. Used to make evidence-based claims about workspace design for innovation and creative industries.

social_behavior.description: Observable social interaction patterns including conversation frequency, prosocial acts (helping, sharing, cooperation), group formation dynamics, and conflict behavior. Measurable outcomes of architectural social affordance density, social encounter frequency, and privacy-sociality balance.
social_behavior.role: Terminal outcome measure. Templates predict observable social interaction patterns from architectural social affordances. Used to evaluate community design, workplace collaboration zones, and healthcare social spaces.

movement_behavior.description: Observable physical movement patterns: walking speed, exploration range, wayfinding success rate, dwelling patterns, and activity distribution across spaces. Directly shaped by spatial configuration (integration values, connectivity) and movement affordances (path width, gradient, visual goals).
movement_behavior.role: Terminal outcome measure. Templates predict physical activity patterns from circulation design and movement affordances. Used to evaluate active design strategies and wayfinding quality.

health_outcome.description: Long-term health metrics: sleep quality (actigraphy, PSQI), cardiovascular risk factors (blood pressure, resting heart rate), immune function markers, and mortality risk. The ultimate dependent variable for environmental health claims — mediated through allostatic load, circadian disruption, and chronic stress pathways.
health_outcome.role: Terminal outcome measure. The ultimate dependent variable for environmental health claims. Templates predict long-term health from chronic environmental conditions. Used to make evidence-based design claims about healthy buildings.

dwell_time.description: Duration of voluntary occupancy in a space, reflecting combined effects of comfort, engagement, social reward, and thermal/acoustic satisfaction. A behavioral proxy for environmental quality; longer dwell times (in non-captive settings) indicate successful environmental design.
dwell_time.role: Terminal outcome measure and behavioral proxy for environmental quality. Templates predict voluntary occupancy duration from combined environmental factors. Used as an efficacy metric for public spaces and retail environments.

physiological_stress_response.description: Acute physiological stress markers: salivary cortisol, galvanic skin response, heart rate variability, and blood pressure reactivity. Measured in response to specific environmental conditions. Distinguished from allostatic load (chronic) by temporal focus on immediate environmental stimuli.
physiological_stress_response.role: Terminal outcome measure. Templates predict acute physiological stress from environmental conditions. Used to evaluate immediate impact of design features on occupant stress in controlled studies.

POPULATION_MODIFIER.description: Individual difference variables moderating the environment-brain-behavior chain

age_group.description: Age-related population stratification affecting environmental processing: children (reduced pattern separation → need for higher environmental distinctiveness), older adults 65+ (hippocampal volume decline → greater reliance on familiar spatial schemas, increased sensitivity to noise and thermal extremes), and developmental trajectory effects.
age_group.role: Moderator variable. Shifts the dose-response curve for most environmental effects by age cohort. Used by templates to generate population-specific predictions (e.g., elderly need higher contrast, more wayfinding cues).

expertise_familiarity.description: Level of architectural expertise and environmental familiarity as moderators of prediction error. Architects generate more precise environmental predictions (smaller PE for typical designs, larger PE for code violations). Environmental familiarity builds richer generative models, reducing novelty-driven exploration but enhancing schema-dependent encoding efficiency.
expertise_familiarity.role: Moderator variable. Adjusts prediction error magnitude based on architectural knowledge. Used by templates to differentiate design impact on naive occupants vs. informed observers vs. expert architects.

anxiety_trait.description: Dispositional anxiety level as a moderator of environmental threat processing. High trait anxiety amplifies amygdala responses to architectural entrapment, darkness, and spatial unpredictability. Alters the optimal Goldilocks zone for environmental complexity downward and increases sensitivity to territorial boundary violations.
anxiety_trait.role: Moderator variable. Amplifies threat-related environmental processing. Used by templates to predict differential impact of environmental stressors on anxious vs. non-anxious populations.

cultural_background.description: Cultural cluster as moderator of proxemic norms, color associations, spatial preferences, and social density tolerance. Hall's cultural zones (contact vs. non-contact cultures) shift interpersonal distance norms by 30-50%. Color-emotion associations and spatial enclosure preferences vary significantly across East Asian, Mediterranean, Northern European, and Latin American clusters.
cultural_background.role: Moderator variable. Shifts normative ranges for proxemics, color preference, and spatial density tolerance. Used by templates to generate culturally-appropriate design recommendations.

sensory_sensitivity.description: Individual differences in sensory processing sensitivity (SPS/HSP scale). High-SPS individuals show amplified neural and affective responses to environmental sensory input: greater benefit from positive environments, greater distress from negative ones. Relevant for design of clinical, educational, and workplace environments.
sensory_sensitivity.role: Moderator variable. Amplifies all sensory processing (positive and negative). Used by templates to predict heightened environmental impact on high-SPS populations (relevant for inclusive design).

clinical_condition.description: Clinical population membership as an environmental sensitivity modifier: dementia (impaired spatial navigation → need for enhanced wayfinding cues), ADHD (executive function depletion → benefit from nature exposure), depression (reduced reward sensitivity → need for environmental novelty), chronic pain (amplified interoceptive precision).
clinical_condition.role: Moderator variable. Specifies population-specific design requirements. Used by templates to generate evidence-based design guidance for healthcare, educational, and therapeutic environments.

openness_to_experience.description: Big Five personality trait moderating aesthetic response and novelty seeking. High Openness individuals show greater reward system activation for novel, complex, and ambiguous environments. Low Openness individuals prefer familiar, orderly, conventional environmental configurations.
openness_to_experience.role: Moderator variable. Shifts optimal complexity and novelty levels. Used by templates to predict differential aesthetic and curiosity responses to environmental design variation.

musical_training.description: Years and type of formal musical training as a moderator of acoustic processing depth, rhythmic entrainment strength, and auditory scene analysis precision. Trained musicians show enhanced subcortical auditory encoding and greater emotional response to structural expectancy violations in acoustic environments.
musical_training.role: Moderator variable. Enhances depth of acoustic processing. Used by templates predicting musical/acoustic environmental effects to adjust for trained vs. untrained listeners.

ARCHITECTURAL_MODIFIER.description: Built environment characteristics and methodological moderators

building_type.description: Architectural typology affecting baseline expectations: office (productivity-optimized), school (developmental-appropriate), hospital (healing-supportive), residential (restoration-focused). Each type carries different normative ranges for acceptable noise, light, temperature, and social density parameters.
building_type.role: Context variable. Sets baseline expectations and normative ranges for all environmental parameters. Used by templates to contextualize predictions within the appropriate typological framework.

exposure_duration.description: Duration of environmental exposure as a moderator of effect magnitude. Acute effects (minutes to hours) differ qualitatively from chronic effects (weeks to years): habituation reduces positive aesthetic effects over time, but chronic stressor accumulation compounds allostatic load without habituation.
exposure_duration.role: Context variable. Modifies effect magnitude based on acute vs. chronic exposure. Used by templates to distinguish immediate perceptual effects from long-term health accumulation effects.

dose_response_function.description: Shape of the relationship between environmental stimulus intensity and outcome measure. Common forms: linear (noise → annoyance), inverted-U/Goldilocks (complexity → preference), threshold (minimum light for circadian effects), and saturation (diminishing returns at high nature view quality). Specifying the function shape is critical for design optimization.
dose_response_function.role: Context variable. Specifies the mathematical shape of the stimulus-response relationship. Used by templates to optimize design parameters to their peak-benefit range (especially Goldilocks/inverted-U).

vertical_position.description: Building floor level as an environmental moderator: higher floors offer greater prospect (view quality, daylight) but may increase isolation, reduce social encounter frequency, and amplify prediction error for height-sensitive individuals. Ground floor proximity enables nature access and outdoor transition.
vertical_position.role: Context variable. Modifies environmental inputs (view, daylight, social access) based on floor level. Used by templates to predict differential effects across building height.

spatial_scale.description: Overall dimensional scale of the architectural space: room volume, plan area, and aspect ratio. Large spaces afford exploration and awe but may impair acoustic intimacy and social comfort. Small spaces promote intimacy and acoustic privacy but risk enclosure stress at extreme compression.
spatial_scale.role: Context variable. Sets the dimensional framework for spatial perception. Used by templates to adjust psychophysical computations for room size effects on behavior and affect.

bridge_warrant_score.description: Confidence in the inferential bridge connecting a neural mechanism to an architectural feature, scored on a 6-level hierarchy: MECHANISM (direct neural evidence in architectural context) > EMPIRICAL_ASSOCIATION (behavioral/physiological data in buildings) > ANALOGICAL (lab evidence extrapolated to buildings) > THEORY_DERIVED (deduced from theory) > SPECULATIVE (placeholder).
bridge_warrant_score.role: Epistemic metadata variable. Quantifies inferential quality of the mechanism-to-design bridge. Used by the credence formula to weight template claims by their evidential support. Not a design lever but a confidence calibration input.

confidence_score.description: Calibrated confidence in a specific parameter estimate, expressed as a probability (0-1). Incorporates evidence quality, sample size, replication status, and ecological validity of the source studies. Feeds into the three-factor credence formula: P(CNFA effect) = P(parent theory) × P(bridge) × P(CNFA-specific).
confidence_score.role: Epistemic metadata variable. Quantifies calibrated confidence in a parameter estimate. Used by the Bayesian inference engine to weight prior distributions when combining evidence across templates. Not a design lever but a calibration input.

effect_size.description: Standardized measure of the magnitude of an environmental effect: Cohen's d (mean difference in SD units), Pearson's r (correlation strength), or odds ratio. Enables cross-study comparison and dose-response calibration. Architectural effects typically range from d=0.15 (small) to d=0.60 (medium-large).
effect_size.role: Epistemic metadata variable. Quantifies expected magnitude of effect for power analysis and practical significance assessment. Used by the inference engine to predict effect sizes in applied scenarios. Not a design lever but a prediction input.

vr_ecological_validity.description: Degree to which virtual reality presentations faithfully replicate the neural and psychological responses to real architectural environments. Known limitations include absent haptic, thermal, olfactory, and proprioceptive channels; reduced field-of-view; and simulator sickness. VR evidence is discounted relative to in-situ studies.
vr_ecological_validity.role: Epistemic metadata variable. Discounts evidence from virtual reality studies relative to in-situ evidence. Used by the credence formula to adjust confidence when evidence comes primarily from VR-based experiments.

METHODOLOGY.description: Methodological and statistical variables that characterize study quality and quantitative findings. These are research variables reported in or computed from empirical studies.

mean_effect_size.description: Average standardized effect size (Cohen d, Hedges g, or r) across studies or findings for a given mechanism or causal link. Critical for quantifying the practical significance of architectural effects beyond statistical significance.
mean_effect_size.role: Quantifies the magnitude of an effect. Used in calibrated_parameters to record evidence strength for each template mechanism.

effect_size_range.description: Range of effect sizes observed across studies [min, max]. Captures heterogeneity in findings — a narrow range indicates consistent effects, a wide range suggests important moderators.
effect_size_range.role: Quantifies effect consistency. Wide ranges flag moderator analysis needs. Used in calibrated_parameters alongside mean_effect_size.

total_sample_size.description: Total number of participants across all studies contributing to a calibrated parameter. Larger samples provide more precise estimates. Critical for assessing statistical power and generalizability of findings.
total_sample_size.role: Quantifies evidence base size. Small total_sample_size flags underpowered calibrations. Used in calibrated_parameters to record data volume.

mechanism_levels.description: Canonical mechanism chain levels used in template causal links. These are analysis levels of description (from environmental stimulus through neural/cognitive processing to behavioral outcome), NOT measurement variables. Used for pathway classification, template matching, mechanism tracing, and BN edge construction.
mechanism_levels.source: Doc 35 (CX-1) Level taxonomy, template.ts Level type

environmental.description: Physical properties of architectural space serving as stimulus

sensory.description: Peripheral sensory transduction (retina, cochlea, skin receptors)

perceptual.description: Cortical perceptual processing and feature extraction

neural.description: General neural activity and network dynamics

subcortical.description: Subcortical structures (amygdala, hippocampus, basal ganglia, brainstem)

neuroendocrine.description: Hormonal signaling cascades (HPA axis, HPG axis, melatonin)

cellular.description: Cellular-level processes (gene expression, receptor binding, synaptic plasticity)

cognitive.description: Higher cognitive functions (attention, memory, reasoning, planning)

affective.description: Emotional processing, valence, arousal, and mood states

behavioral.description: Observable behavior and measurable performance outputs

motor.description: Motor planning, execution, and sensorimotor integration

subpersonal.description: Non-conscious mechanisms below the threshold of awareness

individual_differences.description: Person-level trait variation that moderates effects

calibration_metadata.description: Computed metadata keys that appear inside calibrated_parameters objects. These are internal calibration statistics, NOT research measurement variables. They are excluded from the canonical variable check because they describe the state of calibration, not measured constructs.

direction_consensus.description: Proportion of studies agreeing on effect direction (0.0-1.0)

majority_direction.description: The most commonly reported effect direction across studies

n_supporting_papers.description: Count of papers providing evidence for this calibration

total_findings.description: Total number of empirical findings used in calibration
